messages.subject: Duplicate records in record table when images are 0 seconds apart - is there a fix?
messages.subject_clean: Duplicate records in record table when images are 0 seconds apart - is there a fix?
messages.body_plain:
I have been able to successfully generate a record table and export as a csv, using the recordTable function. I have set the minDeltaTime to 60 minutes, with delta time compared to last record (see code below). However, I am running into issues where multiple records are generated when there should only be one record (given the minDeltaTime of 60).

This is only happening in a specific case: when two images have the exact same date, time, location, & species, they are appearing as two separate records. (My cameras are set to take photos in bursts of 2, with a 30 second quiet period, so as a result, many pairs of images are taken at the exact same time.) Otherwise, the minDeltaTime seems to be working, when there is >=1 second between photos of the same species.

database <- recordTable(inDir = "Merged_photos",
                        IDfrom = "directory",
                        minDeltaTime = 60,
                        deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord",
                        timeZone = "Africa/Maputo",
                        stationCol = "Camera",
                        writecsv = TRUE,
                        removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE)

Anybody else encountering this problem, or know of a workaround?

Thanks!

Best,
Kaitlyn Gaynor
PhD Candidate
University of California - Berkeley

messages.subject: Re: error message when creating detection history
messages.subject_clean: error message when creating detection history
messages.body_plain:
Hi Iding,
this problem is easily fixed. It is the argument day 1 that causes the problem because it begins with a capital letter. Change it to "station" and it will work.

DetHist1 <- detectionHistory(recordTable         = cat_bungo,
                             camOp                = matrix_bg,
                             stationCol           = "Station",
                             speciesCol           = "Species",
                             recordDateTimeCol    = "DateTime",
                             species              = "golden cat",
                             occasionLength       = 7,

                             day1                 = "station",     # changed to lower case

                             datesAsOccasionNames = FALSE,
                             includeEffort        = FALSE,

                             timeZone             = "Asia/Bangkok",
                             recordDateTimeFormat = "%d-%m-%y %H:%M"
                             )

I'm sorry I did not think of this earlier. I will fix it in the next release.
Thank you and best regards,
Jürgen

Hi Iding,
i edited my answer above. It should now work. The problem is that Excel always strips the date/time column of the seconds and the default date/time format will not work anymore. You can either use the code above or restore the original date/time information by pasting the date and time columns with a space inbetween.
You will notice another error coming up:
Error: record date outside camera operation date range:  K042
This is because one of the records is in 2013 whereas the cameras were active in 2014, so this is a problem in the input data.
Hope it works now.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jim,
can you please provide some more details on your question? Did you tag the number of animals in the pictures? If so, with which software? If you used digiKam or Adobe Bridge / Lightroom, it will be extracted and tabulated automatically in the recordTable functions. If you set argument minDeltaTime = 0, you get metadata of all images tabulated.
And what exactly do you mean by report in which you'd like to have the number of observed animals per cameraSite? Please elaborate a little more.
Jürgen

messages.subject: camtrapR 0.99.9 released
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
a new version of camtrapR is online. It includes some of the changes and bugfixed you suggested. Here is the news section.

Changes in camtrapR 0.99.9
==========================

bugfixes
------------
o camera operation: fixed bug with empty entries in cameraCol when cameraCol is defined (reported by Partha Sarathi Ghose)
o recordTable / recordTableIndividual: verbose warnings and better handling of situations in which date/time is unreadable (empty Exif:DateTimeOriginal metadata tag)

new features
------------
  o detectionHistory / activity plot functions: if date/time is unreadable function returns row IDs to facilitate checks
  o activityDensity: warning instead of error if bandwidth estimation fails and argument allSpecies = TRUE (arises with single records, or a few records at similar time of day)

other changes
------------
o exifTagNames: returns name of image from which metadata were extracted as a message

Thank you very much for you help in improving the package!
Jürgen

messages.subject_clean: camtrapR not accepting the date & time in our images
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jürgen,

We’re just doing a small camera trap study, for which your excellent cameratrapR package seems the perfect analysis tool. Though we are having some problems getting the package to read the date & time from our image.

I’ve tagged all 4000 of our sample images in digiKam, but don’t seem to be able to get the package to accept the images – whenever I try to do a timeshift or recordTable errors appear (below). The images are stored at e.g. G:\rawImages\stationA\camera1 and the code I used is below:

testimages <- ("G:/test")

## image shift time

timeShiftTabletest = read.csv("timeShiftTable_test.csv")

timeshift_run <- timeShiftImages(inDir             )

timeshift_run   = testimages,

                                 timeShiftTable       = timeShiftTabletest,

                                 stationCol           = "station",

                                 hasCameraFolders     = TRUE,

                                 cameraCol = "camera",

                                 timeShiftColumn      = "timeshift",

                                 timeShiftSignColumn  = "sign"

Which results in the following:

G:/rawImages/stationA/camera1

Warning messages:

1: running command 'exiftool -r "-DateTimeOriginal+=0:0:0 0:0:1" "G:/rawImages/stationA/camera1"' had status 1

> timeshift_run

1            G:/rawImages/stationA/camera1     0 image files updated

1            8 files weren't updated due to errors

Similarly, after when trying to export the data, the following happens:

export <- recordTable(inDir  = images,

                                 IDfrom = "metadata",

                                  metadataSpeciesTag = "Species",

                                 stationCol = "station",

                                 camerasIndependent = F,

                                 cameraID = "directory",

                                              )

Warning: timeZone is not specified. Assuming UTC

stationA : 117 images

Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "DateTimeOriginal", value = numeric(0)) :

  replacement has 0 rows, data has 117

I’ve attached an image, one of our 4000 camera trap images that causes the above errors. Could you please help us get the images into a form the package will find acceptable as input?

Best regards,

Tom
